title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck tries to axiomatise a tame (modérée) topology through a 'contrée' C = (F, ≤, ≼). Here F is a set of 'figures' (closed tame pieces of an ambient M, such as polyhedra or subcomplexes), ≤ is 'is a sub-figure of', and ≼ is 'is a subdivision of'. The previous page shows that cospectra and supports of objects are closed for both relations, so F-stable parts are automatically sub-contrées.

Definition 1 (sous-contrée, later qualified 'pleine'). A sub-contrée is a subset F' ⊂ F that is:
(a) downward closed for ≤ and stable under finite sups. As such, these subsets correspond to closed parts M' of M via F' ↦ ∪F' and M' ↦ {F ∈ F | F ⊂ M'}.
(b) closed for ≼. This restricts which closed parts M' can occur; it is to be clarified later.
In the left margin he doubts whether more general conditions should be imposed (e.g. without stability under finite sups).

Axiom C6. Suppose F' ≼ F (F' is a subdivision of F) and G ≤ F (G is a sub-figure of F).
(a) There is a unique G' with G' ≤ F' and G' ≼ G. This is the subdivision of G induced by F', which he also calls the sub-figure of F' induced by G.
(b) The sub-figures of G' are exactly the sub-figures X' of F' with X' ≪ G, i.e. X' is supported inside G.
A side remark: for F' ≼ F, the map G ↦ G' from sub-figures of F to sub-figures of F' commutes with finite sups for ≤. A margin note asks whether the axiom is symmetric in ≤ and ≼.

The next page continues with C7_o: every subdivision of a sub-figure extends to a subdivision of the whole figure. He notes that the symmetric statement is false and suggests strengthening C7_o to C7 by a canonical choice of extension.

In PL terms, C6 is the standard fact that a subdivision K' of K restricts to the subdivision L' = {σ ∈ K' : σ ⊂ |L|} of a subcomplex L. Purpose: to build an abstract combinatorial framework for tame topology (the 'topologie modérée' programme of the Esquisse) without fixing a model (PL, semi-algebraic, etc.).
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The definition of sub-contrée is explicitly tentative (margin doubt about the right generality).
The 'commutes with sup' remark needs sups to exist in the poset of sub-figures of F; this is assumed implicitly.
Condition (b) of Definition 1 is left vague: which closed M' give ≼-closed families is deferred ('plus bas').

ideas.what: Abstract structure (F, ≤, ≼) of figures with sub-figure and subdivision relations, and the notion of sub-contrée corresponding to closed parts of the ambient space.
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology / poset-theoretic analogue of o-minimal or PL structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (o-minimality, 1980s); Shiota (axiomatic tame categories)
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic call for tame topology in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the axiomatics are unpublished as far as I know.

ideas.what: C6: unique induced subdivision of a sub-figure, characterised by its sub-figures.
ideas.modern_name: restriction of a subdivision to a subcomplex

ideas.what: Map of sub-figure lattices G ↦ G' commuting with sups.
ideas.modern_name: lattice homomorphism / pullback functor along a subdivision

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an axiomatisation of tame topology by two interacting order relations. Axioms C6 (unique pullback of subdivisions along sub-figures) and C7 (extension of subdivisions, explicitly non-symmetric) amount to lifting/cartesian conditions in a double structure. Whether the axioms should be symmetric is left open, and the general definition of sub-contrée is left undecided.
missed.quote: Je ne sais pas s'il faut prendre des conditions plus générales ... symétrique pour ≤, ≼ ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A model-independent, purely order-theoretic axiomatics of tame/PL topology, with sub-figure and subdivision as two compatible relations, is not standard. It could be compared with o-minimal structures, Shiota's tame categories, or double-categorical treatments of stratified spaces; the content of each individual axiom is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: Each axiom is a classical PL fact. The interest lies in the unpublished abstract framework (contrées), which documents how Grothendieck pursued the Esquisse tame-topology programme. It is notable archival detail but not a hidden theorem.
transcription_corrections: The annotation '[pleine]' qualifies the defined term: 'On appelle sous-contrée [pleine]'.
's'en correspond' is likely 's'identifient' or 'correspondent', referring to the bijection with closed parts M' of M.
In C6(a), 'un unique H' should read 'un unique G' ∈ F'.
The left margin note is roughly 'Je ne sais pas s'il faut prendre des conditions plus générales (stabilité par sup finis) que les conditions ci-dessus'.
'la trace de G' is likely 'la subdivision de G induite par la subdivision F' de F', continued on the next page as 'la sous-figure de F' induite par la sous-figure G de F'.
